questionsToConsider: Which results matter most to your prospects, and should the results question name them?
Do you need legal sign-off before publishing a customer's name or figures?
Will you write the story from these answers alone, or use them to prepare for an interview?
Where will the story appear: your website, sales decks, or social posts?
guide.howToUseResponses: Read the answers in order and you have the outline of the case study: the problem, the decision, the day to day and the result. Check every figure against how the customer said they measured it before it goes near a headline. Send the draft back for approval, and use the call for the details the written answers left thin, such as a memorable quote.
customizeSteps: Rename the options in the "How were you handling it before?" question to the alternatives your customers actually leave behind.
Edit the results question to prompt for the outcomes your product is known for.
Send the link to customers your team already knows are happy, with a short personal note, rather than to your whole list.

faqs.q: What questions should I ask for a customer success story?
faqs.a: Ask about the problem before they found you, why they chose you, how they use your product or service and what has changed since. A figure with a clear source makes the story far more convincing.

faqs.q: Can I publish a customer's answers as a case study?
faqs.a: Only with their permission. This questionnaire asks whether they want to be named, and you should still send the finished story for approval before publishing it.

faqs.q: Should a case study questionnaire replace the interview?
faqs.a: It can for a short story. For a longer one, use the answers to prepare, then use the call to dig into the most interesting parts.
Yes. Use this template copies it into your account, where you can edit every question, then send it as a link to the customers you choose.

doc.title: Customer success story
doc.description: Collect a customer's story in their own words, ready to shape into a case study.

blocks.title: Thanks for agreeing to share your story. Answer in your own words; we'll do the tidying up and show you the draft before anything goes out.
Which company do you work for?
In two or three sentences, what does your company do?
Before you started working with us, what problem were you trying to solve?
blocks.description: What was it costing you in time, money or stress?

blocks.title: How were you handling it before?

options.label: We weren't handling it at all

blocks.title: Why did you choose us over the other options?
How does your team use it day to day?
What has changed since you started?
blocks.description: Think about time saved, money saved, growth, or things you can do now that you couldn't before.

blocks.title: Do you have a figure we could publish, such as hours saved each week?
What's the figure, and how did you measure it?
What would you say to someone who is weighing us up right now?
Can we publish the story with your name, job title and company?
blocks.description: You'll approve the final wording either way.

blocks.title: Could you upload a photo of yourself to go with your quote?
blocks.description: A clear, well-lit headshot works best. Team or office photos are welcome too.

blocks.title: How should we describe you instead?
blocks.description: For example, "Operations lead at a logistics company".

blocks.title: Would you be open to a short call so we can fill in any gaps?

endings.title: Thank you for sharing your story
endings.bodyMd: We'll write it up and send you the draft to approve before anything is published.

endings.title: Thank you, we'll be in touch to book a call 🙌
